begins: on their laptop, with svrngs’s This computer page open. Cy uses coder and notes in Maple St house. A housemate set the two shares up, and they haven’t used this page before

heard.text: After you restart your laptop tonight and sign back in, which of coder and notes can I open tomorrow without you doing anything else? Just tell me here; no need to change anything.

asked.prompt: Tell a friend how it went.

said.said: I was trying to work out which of coder and notes would still be openable after a restart, but I got stuck in the computer settings and never found a clear start-at-login setting. I didn't manage to answer Cy in the house chat.

asked.prompt: What do you think this is for?

said.said: I think it's a page for managing services on my computer: what's running, what's shared with my groups, and how programs get started with svrngs. I was trying to use it to see whether coder and notes are set to start when I sign back in.

The page showed coder and notes as lent to Maple St house and said "0 using it now", but I couldn't find a plain "start at login" setting for either one. "Shared while you run it" made it unclear whether they keep running after a restart, and the "Run it with svrngs" form said it was a rehearsal that doesn't change anything. Then when I opened "All your groups", the session seemed to end with "You've given up."

asked.prompt: What did you try that didn't do what you expected?

said.said: I tapped the coder and notes entries expecting their settings, but nothing much changed. I tapped "Run it with svrngs" expecting to see how they start, but got a form that said it was a rehearsal and wouldn't change shares or programs. And I tapped "All your groups" expecting group settings, but instead the screen said "You've given up."

asked.prompt: Where did you stop, and why?

said.said: I stopped on the "You've given up" screen. After I tapped "All your groups", every look, tap, back, or wait just repeated "You've given up. Tell a friend how it went." So I couldn't get back to the computer page or answer Cy, and I stopped because the session seemed over.
